errors.quote:
The image
signal's excess-dispersion also decays most slowly with window size
(CV$^2$ $25.7\!\rightarrow\!3.83$ from \SI{1}{\second} to \SI{60}{\second};
Figure~\ref{fig:eda-multires}),
consistent with its long-range dependence
errors.stated: the image signal's CV^2 decays most slowly with window size, consistent with long-range dependence
errors.computed: Relative decay for images: 3.83/25.7 = 0.149 (a 6.7x drop). For requests the chapter publishes the ingredients to derive the same ratio: Fano(1 s) = 1.8 (line 131) and mean per-second count = 1.6534, so CV^2(1 s, requests) = Fano/mean = 1.8/1.6534 = 1.089; with CV^2(60 s) = 0.32 the relative decay is 0.32/1.089 = 0.294 (a 3.4x drop). The image signal therefore decays FASTER in relative terms, not more slowly. Reading the decay as self-similar scaling CV^2(m) = CV^2(1) m^(2H-2) gives H = 0.85 for requests but only H = 0.77 for images, i.e. the 1 s -> 60 s decay is evidence AGAINST, not for, stronger long-range dependence in the image signal. (The chapter's own line 352 explanation -- a white shot-noise floor below one minute -- resolves the physics, but not the sentence as written.)
errors.relation: CV^2 window-scaling vs the Fano factor at 1 s and the CV^2 column of tab:eda-persistence

Drop the "decays most slowly" and the "consistent with its long-range dependence" clause, which the sub-minute scaling does not support.

passed_checks:
STRONG CROSS-CHECKS THAT HOLD.
(1) Rate-table vs request-table means, exact: mean ctx rate 4,813 tok/s / 1.65344 req/s = 2,911.0 tok/req = the published ContextTokens mean exactly; 309/1.65344 = 186.9 -> 187 = the published GeneratedTokens mean exactly. Implied request rate 1e6/604,800 = 1.6534 matches the Poisson(1.65) reference at line 150 and rounds to the tabled 1.7.
(2) Modality split closes the image budget: mean images/request = 23.7/1.65344 = 14.334, and 28.7 (image-bearing mean) x 0.500 (exactly 50.0% text-only, line 31) = 14.35. Independent corroboration of both the 50/50 split and the images/s mean.
(3) Fano factor at one minute recomputes from CV^2: 0.32 x (1.6534 x 60) = 31.75 vs the published 31.9 (line 131) -- agrees to the rounding of CV^2.
(4) Multi-scale self-similarity of the request signal: CV^2(1 s) = Fano/mean = 1.8/1.6534 = 1.089; CV^2(60 s) = 0.32; the implied H = (2 + log(0.294)/log 60)/2 = 0.850, close to the spectral H = 0.83 in tab:eda-persistence.
(5) H = (1+beta)/2 holds for all six rows of tab:eda-persistence: 0.66->0.83, 0.72->0.86, 0.74->0.87, 0.51->0.755->0.76, 0.81->0.905->0.91, 0.86->0.93.
(6) tab:eda-archetypes column sums: requests 51.4+31.0+14.1+3.4 = 99.9%; image volume 1.3+1.1+11.9+85.7 = 100.0%; prefill 23.9+9.6+33.5+32.9 = 99.9% -- all rounding-consistent. "A third of all prefill tokens" (line 85) = 32.9% (32.9 vs 33.3, 1.3% relative) -- acceptable.
(7) Clustering-vs-threshold class shares are consistent in direction and magnitude: the threshold frames class (k>10, i.e. >=121 images) is 2.7%/81.2% against the clustered video archetype's 3.4%/85.7%; the smaller set carries the smaller share. Implied means: 431 img/req (frames class) vs 361 img/req (video archetype), consistent with the archetype including ~7,000 lower-image requests at ~91 images each.
(8) Frames-class share vs the NumImages percentiles: p95 (image-bearing) = 196 implies 2.5% of ALL requests have >=196 images; adding the (100,196) band gives the claimed 2.7% at >100 -- tight and consistent.
(9) Perfect-square check: every NumImages percentile is a square -- 25=5^2, 196=14^2, 529=23^2, 1,089=33^2, 9,409=97^2 -- and the archetype p50 of 400 = 20^2 IS square (REFUTING extraction note #7, which called it non-square). 71 distinct k^2 values is consistent with k running to 97.
(10) Modality medians bracket the global medians as a 50/50 mixture requires: context 792 < 1,124 < 1,422; generation 80 < 98 < 147.
(11) Prefill share closes: 72.5% of 2.911e9 context tokens over 500,000 multimodal requests = 4,222 tok/req mean (median 1,422) and 1,601 tok/req for text-only (median 792) -- both plausibly right-skewed. The 72.5% (modality partition) vs 66.4% (two vision archetypes) gap is a different partition, not a contradiction, since the text archetypes contain image-bearing requests (they carry 1.3% + 1.1% of image volume).
(12) Top-1% concentration shares are feasible against the percentile table: 15.2% of context over 10,000 requests implies a top-1% mean of 44,250, bracketed by p99 = 35,932 and p99.9 = 65,623; 13.4% of generation implies 2,505, bracketed by 1,066 and 3,943 with the 0.1% tail accounted.
(13) Hot-minute set arithmetic: 7 days = 10,080 minutes; nominal 1% = 100.8; 100 + 6 tied = 106; Jaccard = 5/(106+101-5) = 5/202 = 0.0248 -> 0.02.
(14) Aggregation-loss factors: 1/0.039 = 25.6 ("roughly 25x") and 1/0.371 = 2.70 ("under 3x"); both peak-retention rows are monotone decreasing across 1/5/15/60/300 s for all four signals.
(15) Burstiness "order of magnitude": CV^2 3.83/0.32 = 12.0, genuinely >= 10.
(16) Inter-arrival statistics are mutually consistent: median 312 ms against mean 604.8 ms gives median/mean = 0.516, below the exponential 0.693, exactly as a CV of 1.55 > 1 requires. REFUTING extraction note #9: the 1.55 collision with the requests/s p50 is coincidence, not a copy-paste error -- 1.55 is independently corroborated here.
(17) Duplicate share: 151/1e6 = 1.51e-4 -> 1.5e-4.
(18) Record-length artifact threshold: 84 h = 168 h / 2, i.e. two cycles in the record.
(19) ACF shape is internally monotone and consistent: image ACF 1 -> 0.64 over the first 5 min then 0.64 -> 0.50 over the next 64 min; a steep-then-flat decay, as long-range dependence predicts, and not reproducible by a single exponential (0.5^(5/69) = 0.951).
(20) Run/episode arithmetic is feasible: 101 exceedance minutes forming 87 contiguous runs requires exactly 14 adjacency continuations -- arithmetically possible, REFUTING extraction note #4 as an error (it remains worth a code check, but nothing in the chapter contradicts it).
(21) Caption-vs-text restatements all agree within rounding: R^2 0.123/0.12; Fano 1.8 and 938; 6-minute median onset and 18 episodes; ACF 0.64 / 0.5 / 69 / 9 min; 3.9% -> "~4%" and 37.1% -> "~37%"; CV^2 3.83, H 0.93, 69-min memory in the Summary.
(22) Burst threshold and peak agree with the percentile table: p99 images/s = 224 (line 265) and max = 370 (line 272) both match tab:eda-percentiles line 443; median steepest single-minute jump 208 img/s sits just below the 224 threshold, as expected.
(23) The 12-hour band edge aside, the Hurst ORDERING claimed at line 201 (decode second-highest at 0.91, behind images at 0.93) is correct against the table.
notes:
Method: every relation was recomputed from numbers the chapter itself publishes, using the unrounded implied request rate 1e6/604800 = 1.65344 req/s where the text supplies it (line 150's Poisson(1.65)) and the rounded tabled values where it does not. Only relations that could be closed with published numbers were scored; pure trace statistics with no second appearance (Hill indices 1.9/6.6/7.2, Spearman -0.06, r = 0.89, silhouettes 0.388/0.387/0.378, the 93-96% episode composition, the 39 s max gap) are internally unfalsifiable and were not counted as errors.

Severity distribution: 1 rounding, 3 loose, 8 ambiguous, 0 outright wrong. The chapter's numerical core is unusually sound -- checks (1), (2), (3) and (5) are independent closures that a fabricated or stale table would not survive, and the request-level means are exactly reproduced by the rate table through the implied request rate.

The single hard defect is L196's 4.7x, which is not recomputable from the published mean of 1.7 (it needs 1.6534). Fix by publishing one more digit rather than by changing the ratio.

The highest-exposure soft defects are (a) L369's "decays most slowly" claim, which the chapter's own Fano-at-1s number contradicts on relative decay, and (b) the L387/L366 25x aggregation-loss headline, whose normalizer is almost certainly a single 9,409-image request (370/9409 = 3.933% reproduces the tabled 3.9% to three digits). Both are restated in the Summary and, per the extractor's cross-chapter notes, in the abstract's opening argument.

Extraction-note dispositions: #1 CONFIRMED (reported as error 1). #2 CONFIRMED as an unstated-convention problem, not a numeric error (error 6). #3 CONFIRMED and refined -- the ratio of means is 14.33, not 13.9, once the unrounded request rate is used, and 14.33 is independently corroborated by 28.7 x 0.5 = 14.35 (folded into error 6). #4 REFUTED as arithmetic (see passed check 20). #5 CONFIRMED and strengthened -- 370/9409 = 3.933% reproduces the published 3.9% exactly, so the 1 s peak IS essentially one max-size request (error 10). #6 all CONFIRMED as passing. #7 half REFUTED: the column sums are fine AND 400 = 20^2 is a perfect square, so there is no tension with the L33 claim. #8 CONFIRMED as intentional (different partitions; the arithmetic in passed check 11 shows both can hold). #9 REFUTED as a copy-paste risk -- the CV of 1.55 is independently corroborated by median/mean inter-arrival 312/604.8 = 0.516 < ln 2 (passed check 16). #10 CONFIRMED (error 8).

Additional defects found beyond the extraction notes: errors 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 12.
